subject: Clarify: billing for resumed streaming sessions / prorated partial outputs
messages:
From: Marta Lee <marta@atlas.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Question about streaming invoices — partial gens + reconnects

Hi Aditya,

Hope you’re well. We noticed a couple of odd line items on our May invoice that look tied to streaming responses. Specifically: when our browser client disconnects mid-response and then reconnects (sometimes it retries the same request), we see charges that look like the partial output plus the resumed output. Can you confirm how Redwood bills these cases?

Questions we have:
- Are tokens billed when they are emitted (i.e., partial outputs count even if the client never received the remainder)?
- Is there any built-in de-duplication or short reconnect grace window that prevents double-charging on quick reconnects/retries?
- If a retry is triggered by our client code (exponential backoff), does that create a second billable session?

I attached a short log extract (atlas_streaming_logs.txt) and highlighted two invoice lines that look duplicated. If you can point us to the exact policy or the relevant rate card language, that’d help us explain to finance.

Thanks —
Marta
Head of Platform
Atlas AI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lee <marta@atlas.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about streaming invoices — partial gens + reconnects

Marta — great question, thanks for the logs. Short answer up front: for the hosted API we bill tokens when the runtime successfully emits them; that includes partial outputs produced before a disconnect. However, we do provide a short session-continuity reconciliation window for rapid reconnects that can dedupe duplicates in certain cases. Details below.

Key points:
- Billing trigger: tokens are recorded and metered at the point of emission on the server side (per-token). If a client disconnects after 200 tokens are emitted, those 200 tokens are billable.
- Grace / dedupe window: if the client reconnects to the SAME session handle (session_id) within 10 seconds and the resumed request references the same conversation state, our backend attempts to reconcile duplicate KV/output chunks and will not charge again for the exact same emitted tokens. This is intended to cover short network blips and TCP-level reconnects.
- Retries and idempotency: if the client issues a fresh request (different request_id/session_id) after a timeout, that new request is billed normally — there’s no automatic cross-request deduplication.
- Streaming SDK behavior: our official SDKs expose a session_id param and automatically reuse the socket/session when possible; if you roll your own retry logic make sure to pass the session_id to benefit from the grace window.
- Edge cases: partial output followed by an edited continuation (server constructs differing token stream) will yield charges for both streams because emitted tokens differ.

Attached: updated rate_card_v3.pdf (section 2.4 calls out streaming metering) and a link to the docs page. For Dedicated/Enterprise customers we can expand the grace window or add reconciliation credits as part of contract terms — happy to connect your procurement/account team if you want that route.

If you’d like, I can escalate the two invoice lines to billing for a manual review while we confirm whether the session_id was reused.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
From: Marta Lee <marta@atlas.ai>

Subject: Re: Question about streaming invoices — partial gens + reconnects

Thanks, Aditya — that helps a lot. Quick follow-ups:

1) In our logs the reconnects do include the same session_id most of the time; I’ve attached the log extract (atlas_streaming_logs.txt) showing two events where the socket reconnected within ~3–4s but the invoice shows both outputs billed. Can you confirm whether those specific request_ids would have been deduped or if we should expect a manual credit?

2) Our SDK currently does a blind retry when it sees a network failure (it creates a new request_id). Are you saying switching to session_id reuse is sufficient to avoid most accidental double-charges?

3) If billing treats emitted tokens as the canonical event, what’s your recommended best-practice to minimize accidental doubled charges in production?

We’re trying to avoid a recurring dispute with Finance — the amount in question this month is ~USD 1,240 and will definitely trigger a procurement review if not resolved.

—Marta
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lee <marta@atlas.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about streaming invoices — partial gens + reconnects

Marta — looping in Laura from finance to triage the invoice lines. Aditya, thanks for the clear summary.

Laura: can you take a look at the two invoice entries Marta flagged (HBSP-45321) and confirm whether a reconciliation credit is appropriate? Based on the logs they appear to be within the 10s session-continuity window, so my expectation is that billing should either have reconciled or we should issue a one-time credit if the backend missed dedupe.

Marta: while Laura reviews, two short recommendations to minimize recurrence:
- Have your client SDK pass the session_id field (our SDK sets this by default).
- On retry, prefer resuming the session instead of creating a new request_id; if you must create a new request, add a short client-side debounce of 3–5s to reduce duplicate attempts.

If you want, we’ll run a short session to instrument a repro and verify server-side reconciliation behavior. I’m also happy to propose a small goodwill credit to cover the $1,240 while we investigate — we want to keep this off your procurement docket.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai
